Exhaustively tried both routes the brief named: (1) Cooperative grid-sync multi-block-per-matrix panel: I FIXED the brief-0 'corrupts at G>6' bug -- it was a writer/reader race on the pivot row P[k,c] (every block read P[k,c] for its dot while block0 wrote P[k,c]-=w); fix = block0 seeds the v[k]=1 term into the global dot accumulator so apply never re-reads P[k,c], plus publish the live pivot diagonal via the accumulator and use per-column accumulator slots. Now correct at all G (factor ~0.003) and SMEM-stages each block's row-chunk (coalesced). BUT it is barrier-bound: ~4 grid syncs/column = ~4n total -> n=4096 b=2 61.5k (geqrf 50.5k), n=2048 b=8 30k (single-block smem 24.5k). More blocks (G) plateau ~66k, confirming barrier-bound. (2) cuSOLVER geqrf for the panel (own handle on default stream; +-lcusolver, portable) + my TF32 trailing: only TIES geqrf for n=4096 (52k) and loses for n=2048 (66k) -- the per-panel-per-matrix geqrf call + transpose overhead eats the TF32 trailing savings. 3xTF32 also retried, still slower. ROOT CAUSE: the (H,tau) compact-Householder output contract forces a column-sequential factorization in the standard basis; TSQR (the one algorithm with O(log G) barriers) produces a hierarchical Q that does NOT map to the flat single-V-per-column (H,tau) format, so it can't be used here. Net: geqrf (NVIDIA's optimal column-sequential blocked QR) is the floor for low-batch large-n, and my TF32 trailing only wins when batch keeps the panel off the critical path (n=1024 b=60 12.3x, n=2048 b=8 3.07x). Committed the correct coop kernel as dormant infrastructure (not routed; would regress).
